summary: L3 validated as a measurement in counted field_ops. The three chain controls (m3 D = 9, 21; m2 D = 57) reproduce the recorded dc2c30a4 cells per target exactly. Validator replays with the new binary and with the frozen binary also match exactly (P5). Each of the 16 flat cells that has a complete chain record shares its six target_x in order. All 354 targets in L1, L3 and the recorded comparators were re-derived from the seed law with independent Montgomery-ladder code. Every consistency flag was re-checked by brute force over V^m with independent summation polynomials. All agree, including the consistent system at flat m2 D = 171. Flat SD = D + 1 holds on all 96 targets (P1). All 16 ratios recompute to the README values (m = 3: 19.5 to 362.6; m = 2: 2.35 to 27.1). P2 fails as written, because D = 27 gives 362.6, above [70, 260]. D = 28 gives 201.0, and every D <= 21 is above 10 (smallest 10.52). The protocol's refutation condition is not triggered. P3 holds (D = 36: 201.6 s in total, longest target 34.5 s, under ulimit -v 6 GB). P4 holds at all nine m = 2 cells (flat/curve 0.98 to 1.25, not only at D = 57 and 133). The non-preregistered fits recompute to 4.40 [4.10, 4.71] (n = 8, span 4.0x) and 2.26 [2.21, 2.31] (n = 9, span 24.3x). Fifteen L3 cells were replayed with the new binary, and all were identical. sub and subflat give the same abscissae (own discrete-log arithmetic and the engine's subcensus, 8 values of D). Major interpretive erratum E1: at m = 2 the flat presentation is slower than the chain in F4 solve time at every D, by 1.1x to 138x. Same-binary controls at D = 57 show 4.1x in the producer's run and 3.3x in the validator's replay. Flat ns per counted op rises from 70 to 14,152, against 3 to 53 for the chain. So the m = 2 'component improvement' exists only in a unit that omits the flat arm's dominant work; it is not validated as an improvement. At m = 3 the direction holds in solve time: 5.7x to 146x across binaries and 5.4x to 9.2x on the same binary. L1 validated, all P1 to P4 holding. p = 16777141 is prime, p = 5 mod 8, p - 1 = 2^2*3*5*279619 with 279619 prime, v2(p + 1) = 1. A = 7842 = 2 mod 4 and A^2 - 4 is a non-square. An independent character sum over 16.7 M terms gives #E = 8*2098009 and twist 4*4192553, both cofactors prime, with r > 2^21. The 10 shared (m, D, k) cells agree to 4 digits (ratios 1.0000000 to 1.0000005, 8 of them exactly), and their SD sets agree. The pre-data amendment (96ac7772bf, 01:35:43Z) is append-only and precedes the first L1 cell (01:35:46Z) by 3 s. Seventeen L1 cells were replayed, and all were identical. Full family rule recomputed: p = 1048261 admits no A in 6..39998 (9,999 values, 100% coverage), and neither do the other six primes. For those six, Hasse makes the r bound unsatisfiable for any A (E6). Errata: README §1 m = 2 range '2.7 to 17x' should be 2.4 to 27x (E2); double rounding of 1.42e7 (actually 1.41e7) and 2.99e11 (actually 2.98e11) (E3); divisor-set wording (E4); the amendment says the engine enforces r > 2^(k-3), but it does not (E5); 'no target finished' cannot be observed in the cells (E7); REPORT.typ/pdf are missing and the figure is stale (E8).

errata.location: README Class paragraph ('L3 is a measured component improvement of the decomposition oracle'), §1 L3 answer at m = 2, §2 interpretation; L3 PROTOCOL decision sentence
errata.issue: At m = 2 the flat presentation is cheaper only in counted field_ops (2.35x to 27.1x). In F4 solve time it is slower than the chain at every D: 1.13x (D = 9) to 138x (D = 189), and 4.1x / 3.3x on the same binary at D = 57. The flat arm's time per counted op grows from 70 ns to 14,152 ns while the chain's stays at 3 to 53 ns, so field_ops omits the dominant work of the flat arm at m = 2. Under the owner's rules (every cost the method incurs belongs in the unit; accounting changes are not improvements), the m = 2 field_ops ratio is not evidence of a component improvement. The frozen decision sentence ('a measured ratio above 1 at every D is a component improvement') is satisfied literally, but its unit is inadequate at m = 2. The README discloses that wall time per op grows with D, but not that flat is slower in absolute time at every m = 2 cell.
errata.fix: Restrict the component-improvement classification to m = 3. There solve time agrees in direction (5.7x to 146x across binaries; 5.4x to 9.2x on the same binary at D = 9, 21), with magnitudes 2x to 3.5x smaller than in field_ops. Report m = 2 as 'fewer counted field operations, more time (1.1x to 138x)', and price the uncounted symbolic work before calling either presentation cheaper at m = 2. The m = 2 fit s = 2.26 is a field_ops slope; the flat solve-time slope from D = 57 to 219 is about 5.3.

errata.issue: For six of the seven searched primes (2^20 - p >= 3555), r > 2^17 with #E = 8r needs #E >= 2^20 + 8 > p + 1 + 2 sqrt(p). Hasse's bound therefore excludes every A, so those searches were vacuous. Only p = 1048261 (2^20 - 315) carries content, with 30 values of A < 40000 failing only the size bound. observations: O1 L1 equality detail: 8 of the 10 shared cells are bit-identical in mean field_ops across primes and family rules. m3 D = 12 and 15 differ in the 7th digit. 'Cost is a function of (m, D) alone' is a generalisation from four values of D (3, 5, 12, 15); it has not been shown at larger D, and the faithful member has no other shared D.

O2 The variation in the L3 ratio across D comes mainly from the chain. The chain's T is not monotone in D (m3: D = 18 costs 2.43e10 and D = 21 costs 2.79e9; D = 27 costs 2.63e11 and D = 28 costs 2.02e11), while flat T rises smoothly (fit residuals are small; s = 4.40 with a narrow interval). P2's upward failure at D = 27 reflects the chain cell's cost, not the flat cell's.

O3 L1 and L3 are stage measurements of F4 on one decomposition system. Neither prices rho or the §5a band, and neither claims to; under AGENTS.md a stage ratio does not establish an end-to-end gain. Nothing here can enter the leaderboard or benchmarks/ without VALIDATION.json, a matched rho reference with the band, and a pcc claim. README §7 already says so.

O4 Wall-time comparisons in C17 mix binaries and host loads (the chain records come from dc2c30a4 in earlier runs; the flat cells ran beside three other leads). The P5 controls bound the binary and load effect on chain solve time at about 15%, small against the m = 2 reversal of 65x to 138x at D >= 133. Wall time is still not a claim of this study.
O5 At m = 3 flat ns per counted op is flat (7.0 to 8.6 ns from D = 9 to 36), so the m = 3 fit s = 4.40 is not visibly distorted by uncounted work. At m = 2 it is (E1).

O6 Process gaps as disclosed in README §7: no Conductor, EKS, S3 checkpoint, benchrec record, pcc claim or VALIDATION.json. Every number remains an unverified assertion with no claim id. This report is one input to the gate, not the gate.
